issues.body: The record still requires the groom lane to resolve a stale differing-value maximum-generation tie by applying the deterministic tie-break, while the exhaustive delete rule permits a maximum-generation deletion only for the deleter's own record when a smaller sibling is present. A later groom owns neither dead writer's operation record. No promotion, delegated-delete authority, authentication rule, or other fenced transition is defined, so the required sweep remains forbidden by the protocol and the disarm latch may remain UNKNOWN indefinitely.
issues.fix_hint: Define a concrete fenced transition the groom is authorized to perform, including authentication, concurrency semantics, and non-vacuous interleaving tests. For example, specify deterministic promotion of the selected value at a fresh generation, or narrowly authorize groom deletion of the selected loser while preserving the never-delete-winner invariant.
issues.title: The stale-tie groom still cannot delete a dead writer's loser

issues.body: Step 0 still says that finding a record carrying `(N, op)` means the operation landed and immediately returns it. It does not fetch or compare the record body with the expected operation body under the declared volatile-field equivalence rule. Thus corruption, an operation-digest collision, or divergent bytes at the same path are silently accepted on retry instead of producing conflict or UNKNOWN. The later test requirement for varying bodies exercises store create-or-keep behavior, but does not close this early-return bypass.
issues.fix_hint: Require step 0 rediscovery to read and validate the existing record using the declared equivalence rule before returning. Divergence must fail closed. Add a restart/lost-response test with a matching `(N, op)` filename but non-equivalent bytes and assert conflict or UNKNOWN rather than success.
issues.title: Step 0 still accepts a matching path without validating its body

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 6 leaves both round-5 soundness gaps materially unchanged. The stale differing-value tie is still assigned to a groom that is not authorized by the stated delete invariant to remove either dead writer's maximum-generation loser; no promotion, delegated ownership, or other fenced groom transition is defined, so UNKNOWN may remain permanent. Step 0 still treats an `(N, op)` filename match as proof that the operation landed and returns without validating the immutable record body under the declared volatile-field equivalence rule. Both defects remain load-bearing, so changes are still required.
